headline: A 2017 executive order calls for a federal review of how well US manufacturing and defense supply chains can hold up to disruptions.
what_it_does: Based on its title, this order directs federal agencies to study the factories, companies, and supply chains that the US military and the wider economy depend on. The goal is to find weak spots, such as reliance on a single supplier, and to look for ways to make those supply chains stronger. No summary was provided, so the specific steps, deadlines, and agencies involved are not described here.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies, especially those handling defense
who_it_affects.how: They are expected to carry out the review of the manufacturing and defense supply base.
Their role as suppliers to the military and the economy is the subject of the review.

when_it_takes_effect: Signed July 21, 2017; executive orders usually take effect when signed.
